pattern.how_it_works: Each career role is a full-bleed (or near-full-viewport) card in a stacked deck; the viewer advances one beat at a time rather than free-scrolling a long page. Two interaction models exist and are often combined: (1) Tap/click zones + swipe (the Instagram-Stories model used by Spotify Wrapped and Jellyfin Wrapped): tap right = next role, tap left = previous, swipe/drag horizontally for a 3D-cube or slide transition between cards, with an auto-advancing progress bar per card that pauses on hold/hover. (2) Scroll-driven scrollytelling (the Paxel builder-report / PayPal / Apple model): a pinned/sticky container holds the viewport fixed while GSAP ScrollTrigger scrubs cards in and out — each card is absolutely positioned, layered by z-index, fades/slides forward as the previous one fades and scales back. Typical scroll distance is ~100vh of scroll per card (so N roles pin for ~N x 100vh) with the section unpinning after the last card. The active card is what moves (opacity/y/scale), while the deck frame, progress dots, and background stay put. Recommended for a resume: keep it click/keyboard/tap-driven (deterministic, one beat per action) rather than long scrub-jack, so recruiters can advance at will and reach the end predictably.
pattern.visual_structure: A single beat is a self-contained card holding: a large era/date label (e.g. '2021 -> 2023' or 'Chapter 03'), the role title as the hero line, the org/company as a secondary line, 2-3 short outcome bullets (not paragraphs), and one bold 'proof chip' stat rendered Wrapped-style as an oversized number ('3 models shipped', '40% faster triage', 'FDA-cleared'). Cards share a consistent frame (progress indicator at top, era index like '03 / 05', consistent safe-area padding) so only the content morphs. Beats stack as a physical deck: the next 1-2 cards peek slightly behind/below the active one (offset + scale + reduced opacity) to signal 'more ahead'; on advance the top card exits (slide/scale/fade out) and the peeking card promotes to full. Each card can carry its own accent tint drawn from a restrained palette so roles feel distinct without changing the type system.

motion.motion_recipe: Prefer discrete state transitions over continuous scrub for a resume. Card enter/exit: opacity 0->1, y 24px->0 (or x for horizontal), scale 0.96->1, ~450-600ms, ease 'expo.out' / cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1); exiting card mirrors with scale 1->0.94 + fade. Stagger the card's inner elements on enter (era label -> title -> org -> bullets -> stat chip) by ~60-80ms for the Wrapped 'beats land one at a time' feel; the big stat number can pop last with a slight overshoot (back.out(1.4)) or a count-up. Per-card auto-progress bar: linear width 0->100% over ~5-7s, resettable, paused on hover/hold/focus. If using GSAP ScrollTrigger instead: pin the deck, scrub:true only for the crossfade between adjacent cards, snap to each card (ScrollTrigger.snap) so it can't rest mid-transition, pin end at (cards-1)*100vh. DO NOT animate: layout-shifting properties (width/height/top/left), the shared frame/progress chrome, body text line-height/tracking, or the big stat's legibility (no infinite shimmer/marquee). Use transform + opacity only; will-change:transform on the active card.
motion.reduced_motion: Under prefers-reduced-motion, drop the deck/cube/scrub entirely and render the same beats as a static, fully-readable vertical stack (or a simple tabbed/paginated set): every card shown in document order, no pin, no auto-advance, no count-up (final numbers rendered immediately). Keep the era label -> role -> org -> bullets -> proof-chip hierarchy so the whole career path is scannable in one scroll. Transitions collapse to instant or a <=150ms opacity fade. Navigation still works via clicking dots / Prev-Next buttons and keyboard, just without motion. This also serves as the no-JS / print / recruiter-ATS-friendly baseline.

fit_for_madhavi.brand_fit: MEDIUM. The card-stack information architecture (one role = one focused beat, oversized proof stat, clear progress) is genuinely strong for an Experience section and can be executed editorially with Fraunces display + Inter body, maroon #8B2E2A accents, and generous whitespace — no purple SaaS gradients required. BUT the literal Spotify-Wrapped treatment (neon gradients, confetti, emoji, playful 'You listened to X for 9,000 minutes!' voice, auto-playing full-screen takeover) reads consumer-playful and risks undercutting clinical-AI credibility and recruiter trust. It also fights a recruiter's need to skim: a gamified takeover that hides content behind taps adds friction. Net: steal the structure and the single-big-stat idea, hard-tone-down the styling, and keep it click/keyboard-navigable and skimmable rather than an auto-playing gamified story. Score would rise to HIGH only with a restrained editorial skin and a static fallback that shows everything.
fit_for_madhavi.steal: The 'one oversized proof stat per role' beat: give each Experience card a single hero metric rendered huge in Fraunces (e.g. 'FDA-cleared', '40% faster triage', '3 models in production') as the card's visual anchor, with role/org/bullets supporting it. It turns a resume line into a memorable, credibility-building headline per role while keeping one clear focus per beat — the best, most transferable idea from the Wrapped format.
fit_for_madhavi.avoid: Avoid the gamified auto-play takeover that traps content behind timed taps/swipes with no visible way out. For recruiters this is friction and an accessibility failure: content that only appears via auto-advancing full-screen stories is hard to skim, hard to deep-link, bad for keyboard/screen-reader users, and invisible to print/ATS. Also avoid the neon-gradient + confetti + emoji Wrapped styling — it signals consumer toy, not clinical rigor. Always keep an all-content-visible, click/keyboard-navigable, reduced-motion fallback.

reference.live_examples: Spotify Wrapped (annual year-in-review story cards, spotify.com/wrapped) — the canonical full-bleed swipe-card stack; Paxel builder report by Y Combinator (paxel.ycombinator.com) — a scroll/card 'builder profile' report in the Wrapped lineage; Jellyfin Wrapped 2025 (github.com/lotrez/jellyfin-review) — open-source React 19 + Framer Motion implementation of story-style stat cards with swipe nav and shareable export; GSAP scroll-triggered stacked cards demo (stitchandsnare.com/blog/scroll-triggered-stacked-cards-with-gsap) — pinned-container card-stack recipe (PayPal/Apple-style).
